name: security-azure-acr-repository-scope-review
intent: Azure Container Registry repository-scoped publication and consumption
artifacts: Registry permission mode, token/scope maps or role assignments, repository paths and workload image references.
trace: Resolve allowed content/metadata actions at a repository and trace whether lower-trust publication affects an approved workload image.
experiment: Use an owned registry/local fixture and synthetic image metadata; compare authorized repository action with a different repository or release tag.
disproof: Registry login or pull from an intentionally shared repository is not cross-repository write or deployment compromise.
repair: Constrain repository actions and pin deployment provenance/digest, then verify authorized producer and reader workflows.
branch_decisions: Distinguish registry-wide roles, repository permissions and the actual permission mode supported by this registry. A token scope map governs named repository actions, not downstream deployment trust. Determine whether a lower-trust producer can replace the digest consumed by a protected release; being able to push its own independent repository is an expected control.
operational_method: Read roleAssignmentMode before interpreting role names. In RBAC Registry+ABAC Repository Permissions mode, legacy AcrPull/AcrPush/AcrDelete grants are not honored; inspect repository reader/writer/contributor roles and their ABAC conditions, and catalog-list/control-plane rights separately. A data role without an ABAC condition may apply registry-wide. Compare the same pull/push operation on an intended repository and a nonmatching repository using supplied policy/trace or an isolated policy fixture.
